Their RGRA variant keeps group-relative advantage and drops the clipping terms. Across standard math benchmarks, RGRA can beat GRPO. Simpler REINFORCE-style training may be the clearer path, they argue.
arxiv-2603-18956: Ducoin and co-authors report on the bright afterglow of a gamma-ray burst seen across many bands. The burst sits at a redshift of 1.411 and recalls a record event from 2022. They gather data from a minute to a week after the flash, all through one pipeline. Two models fit the X-ray to optical light with a structured jet in a steady medium. Both fits demand extreme values. The jets look very strong yet wasteful, with weak shares for electrons and fields.
arxiv-2603-19056: Corbino solves Maxwell's equations with a mimetic finite-difference method in one and two dimensions. Mimetic operators copy key calculus rules on a grid, which keeps the scheme true to the physics. He first sets out the field equations and the classic time-domain grid method. He then shows how the mimetic form yields a compact setup for computing. Two tests follow. One sends a sine wave through a lossy slab. One spreads a pulse in a plane with absorbing edges. All code uses a public mimetic library.
arxiv-2603-19156: Andratschke and co-authors compare ways to rebuild a spectral function from data, a hard inverse task in physics. They test a machine learning method and a new multipoint method for the shape near zero frequency. Both are set against known methods on mock data. They then use real lattice data in a magnetic field. From the rebuilt spectrum they pull out the electric conductivity of the medium. The work shows where each method does well or falls short.
arxiv-2603-19356: Novell-Masot and co-authors set cosmology limits from the first DESI data release on galaxy clustering. They fit the power spectrum and the bispectrum together under the ShapeFit frame. Matter density comes out near 0.310, with the Hubble constant near 68.92. Adding the bispectrum trims the error on fluctuation size by about 20 percent. Fits for moving dark energy and neutrino mass stay close to standard values. No strong break from the standard model shows up in the data.
arxiv-2603-19456: Fang and co-authors hide vehicles from detectors by editing real photos in a controlled way. Camouflage attacks change how an object looks while staying subtle to human eyes. Their method fine-tunes a ControlNet to paint camo cars straight onto real images. One joint score enforces shape fidelity, style match, and attack strength. On COCO and LINZ data, detector scores drop by over 38 percent. Cars keep their structure better than with prior attacks, and the look stays stealthy. The attack also transfers to unseen black-box detectors.
arxiv-2603-19656: A and co-authors build light pseudo-random number generators from cellular automata. They first show that all existing linear automaton-based generators score weakly on equidistribution. That trait measures how uniform a generator's output is. Their new designs combine maximal length automata with time spacing. The automata degrees run from 31 to 128, near computer word sizes. The generators reach maximal period and maximal equidistribution at once. They pass nearly all standard empirical test batteries. Speed and performance rival the Mersenne Twister.
arxiv-2603-19756: Böschen presents tableParser, an R package that pulls tables from scientific papers. It reads XML, HTML, and DOCX files, and PDFs with limits. The package focuses on statistical test results in published work. Its tools compile tables into matrices with captions and footnotes. They can also collapse a table into plain readable text. Decoded codes from captions can enrich the output. A further step extracts standard results into a data frame. It recalculates p-values and flags mismatches.
arxiv-2603-19856: Xu, Murphy, and Josipovic ask whether MLIR is a good base for building high-level synthesis tools. MLIR promised to fix problems the synthesis field had with LLVM. The authors answer from their work on Dynamatic, an open HLS compiler built on MLIR. They share what worked well and what caused pain in practice. Their account covers design choices, tooling, and lessons for other teams. It aims to help builders judge if MLIR fits their own compiler projects.
arxiv-2603-20056: Guan and co-authors link school AI readiness to student AI literacy across a whole nation. Their data join 1,007 vocational schools, about 156,000 teachers, and 2.38 million students. A multilevel model tests direct, indirect, and contextual paths between the levels. Overall readiness showed a positive link to student literacy after controls. Each readiness dimension also helped on its own. Together, they acted as one integrated organisational setup. Teacher-perceived AI capability partly carried the effect to students. General attitudes toward AI did not show a stable transmission path.
arxiv-2603-20256: Zhang and Sun present SciNav, an agent framework for scientific coding tasks with checkable outputs. Science agents often chase open ended problems whose results are hard to grade. Coding tasks instead give executable outputs for objective scoring. Existing agent pipelines lean on heavy engineering and fixed success metrics. SciNav works under tight search budgets with a tree search over solutions. Pairwise relative judgments pick the most promising branches, since comparisons reveal finer quality gaps than absolute scores. Weak branches get pruned as the search narrows.
arxiv-2603-20356: Xavier and co-authors present Agentproof, a tool that checks agent workflow graphs before deployment. Agent frameworks encode tool use as graphs, yet safety checks usually run live. Agentproof pulls a unified graph model from four major frameworks. It runs six structural checks and writes witness traces for each flaw. Temporal policies are tested through a small policy language and automata. In their benchmark, 27% of workflows held structural defects. Over half broke a human-gate policy when it was enforced.
arxiv-2603-20556: Sanchez and co-authors build a tool to flag hospital patients at risk of return. They focus on diabetic inpatients readmitted within thirty days. An XGBoost model trained on cleaned records reached an AUROC of 0.72. Prior visits, discharge type, and blood sugar control were key factors. The team also built a mixed reality prototype. It shows risk level, main factors, and a short care summary for clinicians.
arxiv-2603-20856: Srivastava and co-authors classify white blood cells with a light ensemble of small image models. Sorting these cells by hand is slow, and rare cell types are hard to classify well. Their system mixes three small pretrained models: SwinV2-Tiny, DinoBloom-Small, and ConvNeXT-V2-Tiny. They train three copies of each model and average the outputs. Added training data helps ease class imbalance. The authors report strong results on a hard blood cell data set. They also study errors, such as confusion between myelocytes and lymphocytes.
arxiv-2603-20956: Gunnell and co-authors show that a barium magnesium alloy can supply atomic barium for ion traps. Trapped barium ions are prized for long coherence times and long lived states. Pure barium metal is highly reactive, which makes beam sources hard to build. The alloy does not oxidize in air and stays easy to handle. In a heated oven, it gives barium vapor pressure on the same order as pure barium. They trapped barium ions reliably with both sources in side by side tests.
arxiv-2603-21056: Li and co-authors tackle margin bias in semi-supervised text classification. Self-training methods label unlabeled texts with a model's own guesses, then train on the mix. When label representations spread unevenly, those guesses go wrong often. Their S2TC-BDD method applies an angular margin loss and Gaussian transforms to balance label angle variances. They build multi-class and multi-label versions. Tests against leading methods show clear gains, above all when labeled texts are scarce.
arxiv-2603-21156: Gallardo-Gutiérrez and González-Doña study bounded linear operators whose spectrum can be cut by curves. They show such operators link to classes of operators that admit an unconventional functional calculus. This link bears on a long standing question: must such an operator have a nontrivial closed invariant subspace? They also treat a broad class built from normal operators plus compact perturbations. For trace-class perturbations, the calculus exists and the operator is super-decomposable. The results extend earlier work by Chalendar and by the authors.
arxiv-2603-21356: Liu and co-authors present FluidGaussian, a method that couples 3D reconstruction with fluid simulation. Standard reconstructions from multi-view images optimize for visual fidelity alone. That view ignores body contacts and treats function-critical surfaces, such as aerodynamic ones, like ornamentation. FluidGaussian runs fluid simulations to score surface quality at fine granularity. The scores guide active learning toward views that improve both visual and physical fidelity. On three data sets, visual quality rises and velocity divergence falls sharply.
arxiv-2603-21956: Prasad proves a regularity result for nonlocal parabolic p-Laplace equations, diffusion models with fractional reach. Local weak solutions, he shows, are locally Lipschitz in space, uniformly in time. The result covers every p above one and fractional orders in the stated range. The kernels can be rough, even discontinuous, as long as they stay symmetric, translation invariant, and elliptic. Only a bounded tail for the solution is required. For the linear case, the proof avoids blow-up and Liouville arguments.
arxiv-2603-22156: Kassel and Lévy give a formula for a determinant tied to quiver representations. The determinant belongs to a twisted Laplacian built from a linear representation of a finite quiver. Their formula writes it through traces of holonomy around the quiver's cycles. A general block-matrix identity sits at the core of the proof. They prove that identity in two ways, one by counting and one by generating series. For a graph with a vector bundle and connection, the formula counts weighted cycle-rooted spanning forests.
arxiv-2603-22456: Battini and Milenković describe the ETH Flippers entry to a geometry challenge on triangulations. Each instance gives several triangulations of one point set, and the goal is a central one close to all inputs. Their distance counts parallel edge flips. For small and medium cases they encode the search as a SAT problem with extra bounds. For large cases they switch to greedy local search and edge coloring. The entry placed second overall and proved optimal answers for most instances.
arxiv-2603-22556: Erickson and co-authors test whether a seal-whisker shape makes a better flow sensor than plain cylinders. They mount models with tunable stiffness and damping in steady and disturbed flows. Round cylinders shake hard under vortex shedding, while flatter shapes stay quiet. A passing foil's wake, though, excites the flat models most when its rhythm matches their own. Fitting damping models shows the whisker shape damps less than an ellipse at every setting tested. Less damping means stronger response, which suits a sensitive wake detector.
arxiv-2603-22856: Guo and co-authors estimate rooftop solar panel counts from satellite images for grid planning. Standard vision models use fixed features and falter when regions differ. Roof materials, city layouts, and imaging conditions all shift across areas. Their Solar-RAG framework retrieves similar rooftop scenes with verified labels. A vision-language model then reasons by comparing the target with those examples. Case studies at feeder level show fewer errors in voltage and hosting capacity checks. The method beats plain vision models and standalone vision-language models.
arxiv-2603-23056: Parusiński and Rainer study how stable the eigenvalues of Hermitian matrices are. When the matrix changes a bit, its sorted eigenvalues change in a Lipschitz way. The authors lift this map to Sobolev spaces of matrix-valued functions. For finite exponents, the lifted map is continuous, though not uniformly so. At the top exponent, it stays well defined and bounded but loses continuity. The same picture extends to normal matrices, read in Almgren's multivalued sense. Uses cover singular values and condition numbers.
arxiv-2603-23256: Acharya and co-authors lay out how the KATRIN experiment could hunt for keV-scale sterile neutrinos. Such particles are a favored dark matter candidate beyond the Standard Model. A sterile admixture would kink the beta-decay electron spectrum of tritium. KATRIN already reads that spectrum's endpoint to weigh the known neutrino. A new silicon drift detector, TRISTAN, would extend the search below the endpoint. Simulations show four months of data could probe mixing near one part in a million. Key systematics cut that reach by a factor of 10 to 50.
arxiv-2603-23556: Alencar and three co-authors ask whether nonlinear electrodynamics can smooth out black strings. Four-dimensional black strings carry an axial singularity. The team first extends no-go results from round spacetimes to cylinders. They prove that no purely electric regular black string exists under any theory that returns to Maxwell at weak field. Then they build string versions of the Bardeen and Hayward regular hole classes. Curvature stays finite in these metrics, so a smooth core replaces the axis flaw. Causality and unitarity checks gauge their health.
arxiv-2603-23656: Koide and van de Venn turn quantum process tomography into a straight line fit. They derive an exact information geometry inequality for mixed-state motion, Markovian or not. For one qubit, the bound tightens into an identity. That identity lets them read process traits by plain regression, with no local traps. A full-rank check keeps the answer unique. Negative decay rates in the fit flag non-Markovian behavior on sight. Tests on a diagonal Bloch generator back the method, with care near pure states.
arxiv-2603-24856: Ho and Zaslavsky present SentinelAI, a multi-agent framework for organising Next Generation 9-1-1 emergency data. Emergency data arrives from many agencies and systems, and matching it across sources is hard. SentinelAI treats incident data as a stream of updates, merging new facts at once into a unified view. Specialised agents run a scalable pipeline. One agent ingests raw messages and emits standards-compliant case data objects in JSON. The framework supports cross-source reasoning and composite case building for responders.
arxiv-2603-25056: Litvak shows that a mail agent's system prompt can make or break its phishing defense. He tests 11 models under 10 prompt plans. One model's bypass rate swings from under 1 percent to 97 percent with setup alone. Tuning prompts on strong clues lifts recall, but it also builds a brittle shield. A sender-domain match works until attackers register matching domains and flip the clue. Most wins for attackers follow that flipped clue. He proposes a score that weighs false alarms, and argues tools with outside facts are needed.
arxiv-2603-25256: Kim, Liu, and Manturov build a new invariant for braids and knots called the secant-quandle. Quandles already serve as knot invariants that count how arcs can be labeled. This version grows from secants, lines that cut a knot in set ways. Homotopy classes of plain secants and flat trisecants supply the raw material. The result widens the usual knot quandle. It aims to hold richer shape data than the classic tool. The construction gives knot theory a fresh algebraic lens.
arxiv-2603-25356: Zeytuncu asks what makes an integer arithmetic puzzle hard. He formalizes a class of number-game puzzles and builds an exact solver. The solver lists reachable targets and keeps the shortest build for each. From it he labels over 3.4 million cases by the fewest steps a target needs. Plain learning models guess solvability in part but flub the easy end. A small set of traits from the exact builds fixes difficulty fully. How many inputs a shortest build uses proves to be the key trait.
arxiv-2603-25656: Shen studies operators whose Kippenhahn curves are circles centered at the origin. He calls this trait Circularity. Rotationally invariant operators form one class that has it. For each operator with norm at most one, Shen builds a chain of partial isometries. He asks when Circularity can pass along that chain. He finds a new class, broader than the rotationally invariant one, where it passes at each step. Each member gives a counterexample to the Gau-Wang-Wu conjecture. Shen also proposes a test for rotational invariance in matrices.
arxiv-2603-25756: Vivek, Martin de Diego, and Banavar build a geometric framework for simulating mechanical systems on curved spaces. Classic methods lose accuracy on such non-flat spaces. Their approach uses retraction maps, a broad form of the exponential map. These maps give discrete steps tuned to motion on a manifold. Systems are cast as Lagrangian submanifolds, which gives a coordinate-free base. The framework is worked out in detail for Lie groups. Examples include the rigid body, the heavy top, and a quadrotor.
arxiv-2603-25956: Hojjati and Armanfard present ARTA, a training scheme that makes time-series anomaly detectors harder to fool. Deep detectors can break under small, local corruptions of their input. ARTA trains a detector together with a mask generator. The generator finds sparse time spots where damage hurts the score most. The detector learns to stay stable under those attacks. The masks also explain which moments the detector leans on. On the TSB-AD benchmark, ARTA improves detection across datasets, the authors report. Scores also fall more gently as noise grows.
arxiv-2603-27156: Luo and co-authors present GSR-GNN, a framework that makes deep graph networks practical on circuit graphs. Deep models beat shallow ones on circuit tasks when they can be trained at all. Memory and compute costs usually block that training on large graphs. GSR-GNN combines reversible residual modules with a group-wise sparse operator. The operator compresses node embeddings while keeping task-relevant information. The result cuts peak memory by up to 87.2 percent. Training speeds up more than thirtyfold with negligible quality loss.
arxiv-2603-27256: Dumer and co-authors introduce a kinetic Monte Carlo method for systems with competing dynamics. Multiple dynamical channels run, and how active each is emerges from the current state. A driven antiferromagnetic Ising model illustrates the idea. Conservative exchanges compete with nonconserving single-spin flips. Paired, they hold antiferromagnetic order where the driving field alone would destroy it. The low-temperature phase boundary follows a power-law scaling near the critical field. Mid-range transitions fall in the two-dimensional Ising class. Single-dynamics views hide all of this.
arxiv-2603-27556: Xu and co-authors test object detectors under shifting visual domains. Open-vocabulary detectors find new classes from text labels. That skill often rests on a stable domain premise. Shifts can push image features away from their text anchors. The team defines a protocol for this harder task. Their PICA method trains with a staged curriculum. Pseudo-word prototypes are ranked by quality and trust. Tests suggest stable alignment drives robustness.
arxiv-2603-27656: Kraizberg links prefix-free codes to a class of symmetric trees. Each code maps to one tree in a canonical way. Codeword lengths survive the mapping intact. Some commutative structure survives as well. He then proves a result tied to commutative equivalence. For each code, a prefix-free twin exists with matched power sums. Sums run per fixed word length. A distinguished symbol drives the count. The work adds structure to a known conjecture.
arxiv-2603-27856: Guo and co-authors search for better tree tensor network shapes. Fixed expert shapes miss shifting data correlations. Their HIST algorithm rounds and reshapes input trees. Random sub-network sampling explores the huge shape space. Entropy-guided clustering cuts dimensions early on. Targeted reshaping exposes hidden correlations in the data. Tests span radiation transport and fluid dynamics. Compression improves 2.5 times or more in cases. Scaling stays polynomial in dimension.
arxiv-2603-28756: Kumar and Donatelli speed up model-based iterative tomography for large-scale imaging. Direct methods can add noise and artifacts in sparse-angle tomography, especially for changing samples. Their Fourier-domain framework already used non-uniform fast Fourier transforms and multiple GPUs. New steps exploit multi-level Toeplitz structure in the forward and adjoint operators. A ramp-filtered back-projection gives a smarter starting estimate. A hierarchical approach solves coarse grids first, then moves to finer ones. A distributed MPI version scales near-linearly on large computing systems.
arxiv-2603-28856: Jeanneau and co-authors model lensed galaxies in 3D to study the Tully-Fisher relation near redshift one. Strong lensing boosts spatial resolution, while 3D forward modelling uses faint outer parts well. Their method puts lens deflections right into the GalPaK3D code. Mock tests show it recovers galaxy traits better than methods that ignore uneven magnification. For 95 well measured galaxies, the stellar mass relation shifts by 0.42 dex since redshift zero. The baryonic relation shows no clear shift. Cold gas growth at high redshift may offset the stellar change.
arxiv-2603-28956: Kur and Bizeul study minimum norm interpolation under a 2-uniform convexity assumption. That condition is weaker than a norm from an inner product, and closed form solutions fail. They show the condition yields a bound on interpolation bias for linear and nonlinear models. The bound is sharp for overparameterized linear regression in key cases. They also prove generalization bounds for lp interpolation in a range of p near 2. The work is a first for sharp bounds with non-Gaussian data when the norm is not from an inner product.
arxiv-2603-29056: Ghanta, Gregory, and Calikli study the practical feasibility of sustainable software engineering tools in industry. Such tools are widely studied by researchers, but their fit in regulated workplaces is poorly known. They grouped tools for energy use, green refactoring, and workload control. Each tool was judged on install ease, input needs, and output formats. Workshops with 16 practitioners in a regulated finance firm and a survey of 27 more followed. Practitioners favored tools that plug into existing IDEs or pipelines. They also wanted minimal local data access and clear, actionable outputs.
arxiv-2603-29256: Huffstutler and co-authors build a framework for ruling out quantum speedups. They study partial Boolean functions and their query complexity. Two lenses guide the work: promise-aware measures and function completions. If the promise and completion measures collapse, quantum and deterministic costs stay polynomially linked. Symmetric promises get sharp bounds from one gap parameter. Slice domains get refined bounds. The team derives broad no-speedup criteria for several function classes. Hardness results also limit general completion methods.
arxiv-2603-29456: Wu and co-authors use transport tests to probe magnetism in a graphene sheet. The sheet holds an array of terbium phthalocyanine molecules. Each molecule acts as a tiny single-molecule magnet. At low temperature, the sheet's resistance shows 1/f noise that shifts with field. It also shows conductance fluctuations typical of a coherent sample. Tracking these signals reveals long-range spin-glass-like links in the sheet. Exchange coupling between molecules and charge carriers creates them. The setup suits two-dimensional magnetism studies.
arxiv-2603-29556: Rahaman and Wasilewski ask how big a separable neighborhood around the identity can be in a C-star algebra. The finite case is well understood, but general algebras pose new challenges. They turn the size question into a norm estimate. The norm belongs to contractive positive maps between algebras. That link ties the size to traits of the algebra, such as its rank. As a side result, they resolve a recent conjecture by Musat and Rørdam.
arxiv-2604-00156: Wu models how uncertainty about problem difficulty shapes solving strategy, with an agent brainstorming approaches of unknown quality under a fixed effort budget. Success comes from effort spent on good approaches at a rate set by unknown difficulty, forcing a balance between exploring new approaches and exploiting existing ones. Because a failure may mean a bad idea or a hard problem, optimal search alternates between fresh approaches and abandoned ones. In a principal-agent setting, moral hazard on exploration pushes contracts to frontload incentives, a pull partly offset by learning.
arxiv-2604-00456: Im and colleagues tackle coordination of rival agents facing uncertain costs. A chance-constrained correlated equilibrium lets such agents coordinate through chance-based incentive guarantees. But computing one directly gets out of hand fast, since joint actions multiply exponentially with scale. The authors prove these equilibria equal mixtures drawn from a limited pool of chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria. That turns an intractable program into a tractable one. In large multi-airline tests, their method slashes compute time and beats current practice on system delay costs.
arxiv-2604-01056: Sun and team develop a kernel-based policy iteration framework for team coordination strategies. They consider a multi-agent discrete linear system with quadratic regulation terms and nonlinear safety costs. Building on offline receding-horizon policy iteration, they seek solutions in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, where policy improvement uses a discrete Fréchet derivative. They study the model-free scenario, where dynamics are estimated by recursive least squares and the policy updates from rolling online data. The method is tested in signal-free intersections and validated in SUMO.
arxiv-2604-01656: Jang and Lee propose a design method extending the moment concept from moment matching for fitting to moment assignment for steady-state control. Their core insight splits the closed-loop moment into the open-loop moment plus a compensator-moment term. From this insight, they derive conditions for assigning the desired moment and a standard form for the dynamic compensator. This covers output regulation and closed-loop interpolation, and points to the Sylvester equation alone instead of regulator equations.
arxiv-2604-01756: Li and colleagues present a framework for lip motion in humanoid robots, where lifelike lip sync aids natural interaction. Drawing on Chinese pronunciation theory, they build a 3D dynamic viseme library on the ARKit standard, offering prior lip trajectories. A coarticulation step resolves motion conflicts in running speech using Shengmu-Yunmu decoupling and energy modulation. The team retargets spatial lip motion onto a 14-degree-of-freedom lip system in a humanoid head. Ablations using Pearson correlation and mean absolute jerk validate the lightweight design.
arxiv-2604-01856: Bergmann, Schwager and Berakdar extend quantum confinement theory to sharply bent wires. A particle stays glued to its path, but quantum jitter forbids that picture, so physicists use a potential splitting motion along a curve from motion across it. For such a wire, the authors classify the irregular cases and solve the confined equation for one class with singular Sturm-Liouville tools. Analysis and simulation show bound states pinned at the bend, with kinked wave functions reaching past it, plus scattering states shaping transport and optics.
arxiv-2604-02056: Wang and colleagues handle missing modalities at inference with COMPASS. Completions must preserve the fusion readout. Each modality holds a fixed slot filled by an observed or inferred completion. Fusion matched supervision trains them against real targets at readout level. That means token means for activity recognition and per joint representations for pose estimation. Trained on complete samples, it beats baselines on XRF55 and MM-Fi. It beats token matching for activity and joint mean matching for pose.
arxiv-2604-02156: Alkan, Grezes, Blanco-Cuaresma, Bartlett, Chivvis, Kelbert, Lockhart and Accomazzi release AstroConcepts, a corpus of more than 21,000 astrophysics abstracts tagged with over 2,300 controlled concepts. Label imbalance is severe, with most concepts having few training examples. Baselines span classic, neural and term limited language model methods. Constrained models rival domain adapted rivals, domain adaptation helps rare terms most, and frequency split evaluation exposes patterns that aggregate scores hide.
arxiv-2604-02456: Rubiano computes homological invariants of a trimmed graded double Ore extension of the quantum plane. For a pilot family of type 14641, Rubiano finds the minimal graded free resolution and Betti numbers of the trivial right module, plus linear resolutions for two natural cyclic right modules. The work links PBW structure to homological behavior of natural quotients.
arxiv-2604-02556: Qi, Jiang and Annavaram speed up NF4 dequantization, the step that expands 4-bit NormalFloat weights back to 16-bit form during large language model inference. Their lightweight shared-memory optimization exploits the large latency gap between shared and global memory while using only 64 bytes of shared memory per thread block. It runs 2.0 to 2.2 times faster than the BitsAndBytes kernels across three models, with up to 1.54 times faster end-to-end inference.
arxiv-2604-02656: Wang, Abdeen and Ayer propose a placebo-anchored transport framework for meta-analysis under covariate shift, where trials often misrepresent decision populations. Source-trial outcomes serve as abundant proxy signals, while target-trial placebo outcomes act as scarce gold labels to calibrate baseline risk. A sparse correction anchors proxy models to the target population inside a cross-fitted doubly robust learner for patient-level treatment effects.
arxiv-2604-02756: Liu and five colleagues propose STDDN, a physics-guided framework for crowd simulation. Treating crowds as lone paths invites error buildup and unstable runs, since lone paths miss large-scale physical laws. The framework imposes the fluid continuity equation as a strong constraint. A neural ordinary differential equation models how crowd density evolves from individual motion, keeping path forecasts physically sound. The work targets safety planning, evacuation planning, and traffic systems.
arxiv-2604-03256: Padiyath, Shen, and Ericson test a harm-reduction contract that helps programming students decide deliberately when to use generative AI. Over eleven weeks, 217 students set learning goals, wrote usage rules, and reflected on alignment, with the contract graded only for completion. About 58 percent said it changed their thinking, yet many still dropped their rules under pressure, showing awareness alone rarely sustains behavior change.
arxiv-2604-03556: Kim, Yoon, and Kong study how vision front ends in large vision-language models process visual information in three phases: spread, focus, and respread. They find false object claims are most sensitive to tokens getting low focus in that phase. Their lightweight, training-free fix only quiets such tokens during focus. It uses a DPP to preserve diverse cues while filtering repeat tokens, with tiny added lag.
arxiv-2604-03656: XinYu Zhao and colleagues argue that marketing aimed at language-model answers should stop trusting retrieval alone, since retrieved text can invent facts and send no visitors onward. They model how a model's confidence fades over time and context, then propose routing each user intent to a specialist agent instead of letting the model answer itself. A trial with a meeting-notes product cut task hallucinations to near zero.
arxiv-2604-03756: Javier de Cruz Pérez and colleagues tested whether dark energy truly evolves. They used Planck PR4 microwave data plus baryon acoustic oscillations, supernovae, Hubble rates, and growth data. The PR4 lensing anomaly shrank versus PR3, and the w0wa model still favored evolving dark energy over a constant at modest significance. The authors warn that part of that preference may trace to residual excess smoothing in the PR4 spectra, so the case for dynamical dark energy stays tentative.
arxiv-2604-04456: Sakib and colleagues propose a metric for rationale stability in explainable pattern recognition: whether model reasons stay consistent across same-class samples and input shifts. The team builds the metric with a BERT model on the SST-2 dataset and toughness tests on RoBERTa, DistilBERT and IMDB, using SHAP scores. The metric uses cosine similarity of SHAP values for same-label inputs, flagging biased feature reliance or mixed reasoning for similar predictions. Tests against standard fidelity metrics show it spots off-track predictions and reason gaps, aiding verification of reason stability.
arxiv-2604-04556: Moshayedi sets out a program bridging BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory with Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants of 3-manifolds. He holds that the modular tensor category behind the Reshetikhin-Turaev build arises as the E-2 category from BV-BFV quantization on the disk. A running theme is the mismatch between the compact gauge group of Chern-Simons theory and the group of derived algebraic geometry. The main conjecture asserts a match of the BV-BFV and Reshetikhin-Turaev builds as a topological quantum field theory.
arxiv-2604-04656: Gao and three colleagues study Subset Balancing: given a vector x and coefficients C, find a nonzero vector with dot product zero. The standard meet-in-the-middle algorithm runs in exponential time. The team reduces Subset Balancing with coefficients from minus d to d to a single shortest vector problem. With the best known algorithms, this yields deterministic and randomized algorithms beating meet-in-the-middle for d at or above 15. The team further studies Generalized Subset Sum, reducing its worst case to a closest vector problem.
arxiv-2604-04756: Balogh reads the final MLP layer of GPT-2 Small as a legible routing program, with 27 neurons in a three-tier exception handler. Five core neurons reset the vocabulary toward function words, ten differentiators weed out wrong candidates, five specialists spot breaks, and seven consensus neurons each watch one trait. The point where MLP meddling flips from help to harm is sharp, falling between four of seven and five of seven consensus levels. Tests suggest knowledge neurons act as routing gear, not fact stores, amplifying or damping stream signals.
arxiv-2604-04956: Zhu and Zhu argue that scaling language-model agents marks a shift from tools replacing human hands to tools delegating for human minds. Offloading thinking, beyond the brain's limited capacity, carries thermodynamic consequences for humanity's heat balance. The Earth, they argue, has already passed the heat dissipation threshold for ecological stability. From empirical data, they trace a trajectory and warn that without intervention, heat accumulation threatens world ecology. The paper is the second part of a study on the planetary cost of AI acceleration.
arxiv-2604-05056: Grindstaff and Hoekzema introduce nested tree space, a spatial framework for joint trees. Nested trees model co-evolutionary systems where one history sits inside another. Their sigma-space is a space of nested timed trees with a leaf map, extending the tau-space of Gavryushkin and Drummond. It is built as a cubical complex from nested tree shapes and times of host and parasite splitting events. The authors describe allowed orders through nesting strings in a poset, and show it is contractible and CAT(0), giving geodesics.
arxiv-2604-05256: Archbold and four colleagues propose a plan for studying protest moves while cutting privacy risks. Protest data explain group action but carry high risk, since AI can name people, guess traits, and match photos across sites. Models trained on protest photos risk memorizing and leaking facts, causing cross-platform identity leakage. The plan swaps private photos for labeled synthetic reproductions made with conditional image synthesis, letting pattern study go on without showing real people. It makes varied photos that balance use with risk cuts, and assesses demographic fairness in data.
arxiv-2604-05456: Akoramurthy and Surendiran trim the quantum Fourier transform at the heart of phase estimation. Its full form costs too many gates on noisy near-term hardware. Their phase-fidelity-aware truncated version drops weak rotations below a hardware-set threshold. It shrinks gate counts from quadratic to near-linear scale. On IBM and IonQ machines it cuts gates by about 31 to 44 percent at 30 control qubits with little accuracy loss. It beats full circuits once noise passes a threshold.
arxiv-2604-05756: Jiang and six colleagues test whether language models can match target output distributions over repeated prompts, not just single answers. Off-the-shelf models and standard alignment fail to control gender, race, and sentiment mixes in occupational contexts. Their fine-tuning couples steering-token calibration with semantic alignment, achieving precise distributional control across six datasets.
arxiv-2604-06056: McDaniel and colleagues' 2026 method attributes power and energy on exascale nodes with AMD processors. Sensors there differ in scope, rate, timing, and filtering. Controlled square-wave workloads characterize sensors across up to 512 GPUs and 480 APUs. Power is reconstructed from cumulative energy counters for faster response. After validation against on-chip, off-chip, and node sensors, the method is built into a Score-P/PAPI tool. It separates savings from runtime cuts. Mixed precision cuts Frontier node energy by 79 percent for rocHPL-MxP and 31 percent for HPG-MxP.
arxiv-2604-06256: Xu shows grokking training dynamics concentrate along a few update directions, the spectral edge, separating grokking from non-grokking regimes. Standard interpretability tools miss them, since their structure is not localized. Each direction instead induces a function over inputs, revealing low-dimensional modes. Addition collapses to a single Fourier mode, multiplication only in the discrete-log basis with concentration up 5.9 times, subtraction spans a multi-mode family, and sum-of-squares needs cross-terms for a 4-times variance boost. This suggests training discovers modes shaped by each task's algebraic symmetry.
arxiv-2604-06356: Pouw, Mohebbi, Alishahi, and Zuidema study how linguistic and acoustic features affect in-context learning in speech models. They focus on text-to-speech, asking how accurately the model infers tasks, and how much it mimics demonstration acoustics. Speaking rate strongly affects in-context learning performance and is mimicked in output, whereas pitch range and intensity barely affect performance and are not consistently reproduced. Induction heads in speech-based in-context learning play a causal role. Ablating the top induction heads removes in-context learning ability, mirroring text-based findings.
arxiv-2604-06456: Nowshin, Porag, Jeelani, and Syed build a dialectal Arabic translation system modeling regional and social variation instead of flattening dialects. Their Rule-Based Data Augmentation pipeline grows a 3,000-sentence seed into a 57,000-sentence dataset across eight varieties. An mT5-base model tuned on metadata tags controls dialect and register. NLLB scores about 14 BLEU by defaulting to the Modern Standard mean, while theirs scores about 8 BLEU but fits varieties better. Cultural authenticity rates their output 4.8 out of 5 against 1 for baselines, so metrics underrate dialect fidelity.
arxiv-2604-06756: Tu, Ni, and Bi test how reasoning chains sway language-model judges of factuality. Models now judge answers, yet remain imperfect and open to surface bias, and showing a generator's reasoning might sharpen or distort verdicts. Weak judges bend easily, often accepting wrong answers wrapped in fluent reasoning, while strong judges partly use reasoning as evidence yet still fall for high-quality chains. Controlled tests show both fluency and factuality drive verdicts, pointing to a need for judges that tell genuine reasoning quality apart from smooth talk.
arxiv-2604-07156: Rowland and four colleagues study how to measure energy in near-term quantum computing with fewer wasted shots. They let the same operator appear in several compatible measurement groups, a trick called overlapped grouping. They prove this can cut variance in proportion to the number of terms in the energy expression. Their repacking routine converts old groups into overlapped ones, and simulations up to 44 qubits show the advantage growing with problem size.
arxiv-2604-07356: Smith and 16 colleagues heat natural olivine up to 1500 degrees Celsius and track how its phases change. They tag phase-specific infrared bands with adjustable red-green-blue colors, measured at the Australian Synchrotron. Matching polarized infrared spectra against X-ray composition data and magnetization shows the phase shifts step by step. After heating, the samples gain magnetism as iron-rich oxides form within them.
arxiv-2604-07556: Savale computes the eta invariant of the spin-c Dirac operator over the unit circle-bundle over a positive line bundle on a Fano manifold of even complex dimension. The value is expressed through Zhang's value for its adiabatic limit. This extends the author's earlier computation from small to arbitrary adiabatic-parameter values, completing the eta invariant calculation across the full parameter range for this class of bundles. The work gives a clean closed form for a hard spectral quantity.
arxiv-2604-07656: Aggarwal and five colleagues present MVOS_HSI, an open-source Python library for leaf hyperspectral data. Hyperspectral imaging captures hundreds of narrow bands per pixel, revealing plant biochemistry and stress missed by standard cameras, but labs still rely on loose lab-specific scripts that are hard to share. MVOS_HSI handles calibrating ENVI files and clipping leaves using NDVI, CIRedEdge, and GCI indices. It adds data augmentation and profile tools, and runs as a library or from the command line. One package helps researchers produce consistent plant phenotyping results.
arxiv-2604-07756: Lee and Li study how robust fixed-effects models are for longitudinal cluster trials. Designs include stepped-wedge and crossover trials, spanning randomized and quasi-experimental variants. They correct a long-held myth: fixed-effects models, often thought to target only finite-sample conditional means, can target super-population marginal means through M-estimation. Linear and log-link models with correctly set treatment-effect shapes yield consistent, asymptotically normal estimators for flexibly defined effects, even under arbitrary misspecification.
arxiv-2604-07956: Yüksel and five colleagues present MONETA, the first multimodal benchmark for industry classification with geographic information. These schemes anchor public and company databases, but manual labeling of huge registers costs dearly, and retraining models for every update demands fresh data. MONETA replicates expert checks from existing mixed resources, pairing text from web pages, Wikipedia, and Wikidata with OpenStreetMap and orbital photos. Its dataset covers 1,000 European firms across 20 activity tags under EU NACE rules. A training-free baseline scores 62.10 percent with open models and about 74 percent with closed models.
arxiv-2604-08056: Pang and three colleagues automate the choice of aggregation strategy in federated learning. Models train collaboratively without centralizing data, yet the choice matters greatly. Performance varies widely across data, heterogeneity levels, and compute constraints. Their end-to-end framework runs in two modes. In single-trial mode, language models infer suitable options from user-given or auto-found data traits. In multi-trial mode, a lightweight genetic search tries alternatives under tight budgets. Experiments across diverse data show stronger robustness and generalization under non-IID conditions.
arxiv-2604-08156: Plecháč and nine colleagues investigate how much training data unsupervised rhyme recognition needs, using RhymeTagger across seven languages. Rhyme seems simple, yet scholars struggle with rhyme sorting and people disagree on whether two words rhyme. That tangles auto rhyme spotting and evaluation across tongues. RhymeTagger, a tongue-free tool, finds rhymes from shared patterns in poetry corpora. Scores are tested across Czech, German, English, French, Italian, Russian, and Slovene, testing how training size and language gaps affect scores. Annotator match on a hand-marked subset sets a real benchmark.
arxiv-2604-08456: Marcel Gröpl and four colleagues frame visual grounding in vision language models as evidence retrieval at test time, with no extra training. Their method turns the model's own next token uncertainty into a relevance map over image tokens. It then ranks coherent regions and zooms in again until a spatial entropy rule says stop. Tests on seven benchmarks across four model designs show steady gains, largest where fine detail and high resolution matter, with clearer evidence locations.
arxiv-2604-08556: Singh probes what simple exponential moving average traces can and cannot encode in sequence models, using them as the plainest recurrent context. A Hebbian design with multi timescale traces reaches 96 percent of a supervised BiGRU on grammatical role assignment with no labels, beating it on structure dependent roles. Yet traces erase token identity: a 130 million parameter model using only EMA context reaches perplexity 260, eight times GPT-2's, a gap no downstream predictor can undo.
arxiv-2604-08756: Martin and three colleagues formalize how an environment can serve as an agent's memory in reinforcement learning. They prove certain observations, called artifacts, can cut the information needed to represent history. Experiments with spatial paths confirm agents need less memory to learn strong policies when they observe paths. The effect arises implicitly through the sensory stream, and the findings satisfy qualitative properties used to ground external memory accounts, pointing toward principled environment as memory designs.
arxiv-2604-08956: Kethavath and Hu test whether prompting or light fine-tuning adapts vision-language models better to satellite cloud mapping, where both pictures and wording sit far outside natural-image training. Prompting, the usual route, assumes clever wording can steer a frozen model, but their experiments show small amounts of labeled data win instead. Low-rank fine-tuning beats prompting by 0.03 to 0.09 on the overlap score. The widest gaps fall on spectrally ambiguous cloud types, though tiny labeled sets first dip in performance before recovering.
arxiv-2604-09256: Schultzberg defends Bonferroni correction for online experimentation, a choice better than its reputation suggests. First, it is the simplest broadly usable method controlling family-wise error that also gives simultaneous confidence intervals for every metric. Guardrail metrics use intersection-union logic and cannot inflate false positives, so the family counts success metrics only. It is uniquely tractable for pre-experiment sample size calculations. From simulations and 1,296 Spotify experiments, power loss versus fancier methods depends on family specification and how many metrics are truly non-null.
arxiv-2604-09356: Ghoshal, Jeesun, and Kohri study CMB signs of gravity-carried dark radiation in delta N-effective. Data on N-effective from Planck 2018 and BBN already limit link strengths of light bits beyond the Standard Model. Despite tiny non-gravity couplings, such ones are always made in the early cosmos through gravity, and a lasting density may act as dark radiation adding to N-effective. The authors analyze scalar dark Higgs and vector dark photon cases, finding limits on reheat heat and equation rule from Planck 2018.
arxiv-2604-09456: Lin and Hu compute quantum radiation from wave packets of single electrons near light speed, at rest and under uniform acceleration. An electron at rest gives off nothing at all. An accelerated electron gives off ever more power over long times. The authors read this growth in classical terms, arguing the late-time total stays finite. They also check Unruh-effect searches in spots where classical theory predicts no signal. The quantum shifts there trace to transverse deviation correlators, not to the Unruh effect in electron microscopes.
arxiv-2604-09656: Ruffle and seven colleagues assess the equity of 18 brain-tumour segmentation models, tested on 648 glioma patients, 11,664 inferences in all. Patient identity explains more performance gaps than model choice. Tumour grade, molecular diagnosis, and extent of resection predict accuracy better than architecture. A voxel-wise spatial analysis finds local biases across models and weak spots in lesion and patient-mix feature space. Newer models trend fairer, but none offers a fairness proof. The team releases Fairboard, a no-code dashboard for watching medical-imaging equity.
arxiv-2604-09856: Badoux and three co-authors investigate the circumbinary disk around stellar binary D9 orbiting the supermassive black hole Sgr A*. The team couples a gravity solver for the binary, feeling Sgr A*, with a disk solver using AMUSE. They find the disk settles between about five inner semi-major axes and about a quarter of a Hill radius of the binary. The disk's inclination follows the binary's, evolving through the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai mechanism induced by Sgr A*. The disk's mean eccentricity runs roughly opposite to the binary's eccentricity.
arxiv-2604-09956: Mazzetti and four co-authors present a compiler assigning program qubits to logical qubits in high-rate quantum codes, where each code holds several logical qubits. Brute-force search over mappings is super-exponential. Their framework compiles gates into encoded implementations using Hadamard commutation and gate merging, then searches mappings with a noise-biased packing heuristic. Across 71 benchmark circuits, depth falls 34 percent, and one- and two-qubit gate counts fall up to 31 and 17 percent. Total variation distance improves 1.75 times, with logical selection rates up 86 percent on average over naive compilation.
arxiv-2604-10156: Xiong and Xiong ease the fermion sign problem, the main obstacle to simulating fermionic thermodynamics. Sign-blocking leaves Monte Carlo importance sampling unchanged. Sign-blocking instead applies in post-processing of signed samples. The two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model is the benchmark, given many energy benchmarks. Results match leading benchmarks very well, even in hard regimes. The mechanism is the link between energy and sign factors found through data blocking, inferring system energy. The method promises much for complex quantum systems, especially alongside auxiliary-field methods.
arxiv-2604-10556: Guo and Tan compare invented facts in diffusion versus standard language models. Diffusion models write all at once instead of word by word, yet their truth habits stayed murky. In matched tests, diffusion models invent more than standard rivals of like size and training. Step by step decoding stalls early, while free order decoding keeps refining without end. Distinct diffusion slips include early stops, half cleaned noise, and stray context leaks.
arxiv-2604-10656: McDonald shows how to estimate ages and masses of asymptotic giant branch stars, elderly stars shedding their outer layers, by placing each star on the period-luminosity diagram and comparing with evolutionary models. For Milky Way samples the method yields age errors of roughly 30 percent and initial-mass errors near 14 percent, though accuracy for single stars depends on position and measurement error. Applied to Gaia, NESS, DEATHSTAR, and ATOMIUM samples, it finds most samples skew young and massive, with a typical Milky Way AGB mass near 1.1 solar masses.
arxiv-2604-10756: Wrobel, Landowska, and Makuch study how people prefer emotions visualized in information systems, testing color, size, speed, shape, and animation type. Asking 419 participants about their preferences, they find color, speed, and size track selected discrete emotion labels, while speed also tracks arousal in a dimensional model. The work is a first step toward a universal emotion representation for information systems, linking visual choices to both discrete and dimensional emotion models.
arxiv-2604-11556: Ding, Wang, and Chen present FM-Agent, the first framework for automated compositional reasoning about large-scale systems. Hoare logic splits a system into components, but writing a formal specification per function burdens humans heavily, worse when code comes from LLMs. FM-Agent derives each function's specification top-down from caller expectations, so specs reflect developer intent even when implementations are buggy. It then reasons about functions against natural-language specifications rather than formulas alone.
arxiv-2604-11856: Zhang, Hong, Wang, and Sun develop RAPRAL, a C++ radiation solver for high-temperature flows not in chemical balance, mixing ray tracing with line-by-line spectral models. It covers both fine spectral detail and spatial energy flow. Tests on atom and molecule spectra match a known code across wide settings. Applied to rear heating in the Fire II flight test, using a two-temperature, 11-species air flow, it gives reliable heat-flux forecasts and captures the main heat-flow ways.
arxiv-2604-12056: Xi and eleven colleagues propose LoSA, sparse attention for diffusion language models generating tokens freely. Naive sparse attention fails through KV inflation, as different queries pick different prefix positions, ballooning accessed pages. Between denoising steps, few active tokens change much, while stable tokens stay nearly constant. LoSA reuses prefix-attention for stable tokens and sparse attention only for active tokens, shrinking KV indices. Across models and benchmarks it preserves dense accuracy, gaining up to 9 points at aggressive sparsity, 1.54 lower density, and up to 4.14 speedup on RTX A6000 cards.
arxiv-2604-12356: Yu and five colleagues introduce OmniFood8K, a food dataset of 8,036 samples with detailed nutrition labels and multi-view images, filling thin coverage of Chinese dishes and freeing methods from depth sensors. They add NutritionSynth-115K, a large synthetic set with varied mixes and exact labels. Their single-image system predicts a depth map, refines it with a scale-shift residual adapter, fuses RGB and depth traits in the frequency domain, and predicts nutrition through a mask-based head. Tests show it beats existing approaches.
arxiv-2604-12756: Claudio Gutierrez and Daniel Hernández argue the Web's meaning as a research object has diluted. The Web grew from a focused tech object into a universal digital world. That very success split its academic community and blurred its core identity. Crises at the Web Conference and Semantic Web Conference illustrate the trend. Pressures include the academic tragedy of the commons and disruptive AI. The authors chart the path from a clear object to a split backdrop. A community discussion is needed on what studying the Web means now.
arxiv-2604-13156: Fei, Li, Liu, and Pospelov study the radiative decay of the Z boson into two muons plus a photon at the LHC. Their work gives precision Standard Model analysis and new-physics projections. From Run-1 data they extract a fiducial branching ratio of 3.34 times 10 to the minus 4, and show the mode can be measured to sub-percent statistical precision. The channel also probes axion-like particles and an anomalous gauge boson coupled to muons, extending collider reach down to couplings near 10 to the minus 3.
arxiv-2604-13256: Khudoyberdiev and Bekov tackle shortcut learning in T-cell receptor binding guesses, where models exploit peptide length bias or gene pairing instead of the real binding surface. Their Counterfactual Invariant Prediction framework makes lifelike limited counterfactual peptide edits, keeping invariance at non-anchor positions while raising response at MHC anchor spots. On a curated VDJdb-IEDB benchmark under family-held-out tests, it reaches AUROC 0.831 and consistency 0.724. That is a 39.7 percent cut in shortcut index against the plain baseline.
arxiv-2604-13356: Feng and four colleagues propose Peer-Predictive Self-Training, a label-free way for language models to improve together without external supervision. Models answer sequentially, and their aggregated answer, usually more reliable than any single response, serves as an internal reference. Each intermediate response is scored by pointwise mutual information against the aggregate, so aligned responses receive smaller updates and misaligned ones larger updates. On maths reasoning benchmarks it lifts exact-match accuracy by two to four percentage points and shrinks the generator-verifier gap substantially.
arxiv-2604-13456: Pallerla, Mahmoudi, and Wang introduce MyoVision, a phone-based tool for detecting chicken breast myopathies without cutting or costly lab imaging. Woody Breast and Spaghetti Meat harm meat quality, yet checks rely on manual judgement or costly systems. MyoVision takes 14-bit RAW transillumination images, pulls texture signs of internal defects, and sorts Normal, Woody Breast, and Spaghetti Meat with a neuroevolution-optimized ensemble. On 336 fillets it reaches about 82 percent test accuracy, matching hyperspectral systems costing far more.
arxiv-2604-13556: Wu and eight colleagues improve YOCO, a technique that saves memory in large language models by sharing key-value data across layers. Their YOCO++ adds a weighted residual link from each lower-half layer back to the bottom layer, raising model capacity without extra training or inference cost. At half the usual key-value cache size, it leads competing cross-layer compression methods and beats the standard Transformer in their tests.
arxiv-2604-13656: Tan and Zhao prove that ordinary least squares sits inside the Transformer. They choose parameters from a spectral split of the empirical covariance, inside a single-layer linear Transformer. With those parameters, one forward pass of attention reproduces the least-squares projection. Attention thus solves that old statistical problem directly. In short, a familiar stats tool turns out to live inside a modern neural net. It also shows slow and fast memory inside Transformers, and traces a path to standard models with exponential Hopfield memory.
arxiv-2604-14156: Kiruluta joins two usually distinct ways of shrinking large language models: static pruning and prompt trimming. His compressed-sensing setup probes hidden model use with random measurements, recovers task- and token-adaptive support sets, and turns them into hardware-efficient sparse execution paths. The design adds task-conditioned measurements, token-adaptive recovery, sample-complexity bounds, GPU-friendly limits, and a joint goal joining prompt compression with model reduction.
arxiv-2604-14556: Xia's team of six tackles video object insertion, where a user-chosen object must sit in a moving scene. Text or single-image prompts leave looks underconstrained across viewpoints, causing identity drift, wrong layering, boundary artifacts, and flicker. Their system lifts a 2D image into a multi-view form, using matching-view prompts for stable identity and adaptive cues, while quality-aware weighting downweights noisy rebuilds. An Integration-Aware Consistency Module then aids plausible occlusion, clean edges, and time flow, beating rivals on quality, control, looks, and blending.
arxiv-2604-14856: Allein, Pineda-Castañeda, Rocci, and Moens present ClimateCause, an expert-tagged dataset of higher-order causal patterns from science-for-policy climate reports, with implicit and nested causality. Cause-effect phrases are cleaned and split into single causal links for graph building, with labels for cause-effect correlation, link type, and place-time context. The dataset supports reading-ease scoring from the meaning depth of causal graphs behind a statement. Testing large language models on correlation judgments and causal-chain thinking shows the latter is the key challenge.
arxiv-2604-14956: Wang and nine others introduce FedGUI, the first benchmark for federated GUI agents across mobile, web, and desktop platforms. Centralized GUI-agent training faces steep cost and scale limits, while federated learning lacks benchmarks capturing real cross-platform heterogeneity. FedGUI offers six curated datasets covering cross-platform, cross-device, cross-OS, and cross-source heterogeneity. Tests show cross-platform collaboration improves performance beyond mobile-only federated learning, with platform and OS the most influential factors. The benchmark gives the community a foundation for scalable, privacy-preserving GUI agents.
arxiv-2604-15156: Rose and others map the Raman-active modes of orthorhombic LaInO3 by mixing angle-resolved Raman spectra with theory. Scattering from many crystal faces, read through symmetry, assigns most zone-center phonons to point-group classes. A full-spectrum fit extracts Raman tensor elements from strengths that vary with angle, even where modes overlap. Theory yields phonon dispersions, densities of states, and shift patterns that match lab data well.
arxiv-2604-15356: Magarshak argues that per-vector compression limits miss the real problem in transformer KV caches, since cached tokens come from the very language the model predicts well. His two-layer scheme first merges shared prefixes across sessions via probabilistic language tries, then stores only each new vector's gap from the model's own prediction. The Shannon-limit ratio over TurboQuant reaches about 914,000 times, and stays near 914 times even under deliberately pessimistic overhead.
arxiv-2604-15556: Savir, Fang, and Sulam show how to learn proximal operators that are exact by proof while respecting shift and scale equivariance. Their Affine-Equivariant Learned Proximal Networks parametrize neural functions that yield exact proximals under data-driven, possibly non-convex regularizers. Tests on made-up cases and fresh denoising tasks show tougher behavior under new noise and affine shifts far beyond training, widening the everyday use of learned proximals.
arxiv-2604-15656: Chen, Wang, and Zhang pin down plus and minus 3-energies of graphs, sums of cubed plus-side and minus-side eigenvalues. They prove each linked n-node graph bar K1, K2, and P3 clears root-five-over-two times n in plus 3-energy. This settles a guess for p equals 3. They also prove each linked n-node graph clears the full graph's minus p-energy for all p at or past 3, beating the old p at or past 4 mark.
arxiv-2604-15856: Ulku, Akagündüz, and Tanrıöver present CBC-SLP, a model for multispectral semantic segmentation that copes when some sensor inputs are missing. Standard shared-representation models can lose modality-specific detail and even slip when all inputs are present. Their structured latent projection splits latent features into shared and modality-specific parts, then routes them to the decoder based on which modalities are available. Tests on three remote sensing image sets show it beats leading models in both full and missing-modality cases.
arxiv-2604-16356: Rahman, Shuva, Tripathi, Liu, and Reed propose a machine learning and smartphone-assisted framework for real-time uplink performance prediction in a private 5G system. Using a radio test setup, with an srsRAN 5G stack on a Dell workstation as base and core at 3.4 GHz, they use two Pixel 7a phones for uplink metrics such as channel quality, coding, throughput, timing, and error rate. Tests span stationary, pedestrian, and mobile cases. They cover line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight settings, plus YouTube and server tests.
arxiv-2604-16456: Modi, Mahajan, Wetter and Welles built EchoChain, a benchmark for voice assistants that must update their plans when users interrupt mid-sentence. Existing spoken-dialog tests mostly use tidy turns and miss this failure mode. EchoChain injects interruptions at a fixed point in assistant speech and names three recurring faults: contextual inertia, interruption amnesia and objective displacement. In a paired control without interruptions, failures fell by about 40 percent, and no tested real-time voice model passed more than half the cases, leaving large room for improvement.
arxiv-2604-16656: Mehta and colleagues tackle token splitting: non-Latin-script tongues need several times more tokens than English. Tokens set cost and latency, so the gap taxes speakers of those tongues. The standard remedy, wordlist growth, adds missing target items to the model's wordlist. They advance insight-based growth, challenging count-based item choice. Insight-based methods beat count methods on the quality-token value trade-off. Insight-based vector setup gains about 20 points over rivals for several non-Latin-script tongues.
arxiv-2604-16956: Jonckheere and Shneer study particle systems where reactions and diffusion drive fronts, the moving boundaries of spreading populations. As particle counts grow large, a mean-field limit describes the bulk, and they characterize its traveling waves through tagged-particle distributional equations. The method recovers known Fisher-KPP waves for Brownian particles, extends a compound Poisson model beyond exponential jumps, and links a power-of-2 growth model to the synchronization cases.
arxiv-2604-17256: Paul and Alsmadi introduce the Unified Compliance Aggregator, a framework that folds several Linux security tools into one score from 0 to 100. It combines Lynis, OpenSCAP with STIG and CIS profiles, AIDE, Tripwire, and Nmap NSE, normalizing outputs onto one scale before weighted aggregation, with a logarithmic model for file integrity. Ubuntu 22.04 experiments across hardening levels show scores rising as systems harden, while compliance and file integrity tools behave contrastingly. Case studies on a basic web server and a DVWA-based system show practical application.
arxiv-2604-17356: Mao settles two conjectures from 1981 on Ramsey-finiteness for pairs of graphs, due to Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp. Mao proves that adjoining disjoint matchings preserves Ramsey-finiteness, and shows finiteness survives only in narrow cases: pairs of odd stars, pairs with a two-vertex component, and Faudree's star-forest family. Mao also corrects Burr's stronger 1979 survey claim with the true necessary-and-sufficient form. The result closes a long-standing classification question for graph pairs.
arxiv-2604-17656: Lokegaonkar and seven colleagues present Video-Robin, a text-guided video-to-music model for fast, high-quality, meaning-matched background music. Recent video-to-music models rely on visual cues alone and offer limited meaning and style control. Video-Robin balances musical fidelity and meaning by pairing autoregressive planning with diffusion-based building. An autoregressive module aligns visual and textual inputs into high-level music latents for global structure, refined by local Diffusion Transformers into clear, high-quality music. The design gives creators fine control without losing audio quality.
arxiv-2604-17756: Liu and three colleagues prove a closed-form upper bound on concurrence at fixed local polarizations in two-qubit systems, showing maximal concurrence is set by both polarizations. Pure states hit the bound in certain cases with matching polarizations. Applied to parity-violating e+e- to Z0 to q qbar, which generates final-state spin polarization, maximal concurrence peaks in certain kinematic regions and is much reduced versus the unpolarized case. The results give a process-free framework linking local polarization, maximal entanglement, and pure states.
arxiv-2604-17856: Miyazaki and five colleagues tackle plankton segmentation in crowded images, where labeled data are scarce and plankton hide among debris and overlaps. They synthesize labeled images by placing individual plankton on varied backgrounds. Then they train a Vision Transformer model with a Mask2Former decoder, pretrained by masked autoencoding on unlabeled specimens. On real datasets the method beats older approaches such as Mask R-CNN, especially where debris is dense, while needing fewer manual labels.
arxiv-2604-17956: Wan and two colleagues propose a RuleFit method for medical data shared across sites, letting institutions train without sharing raw records. Privacy rules and ownership limits block pooled data, while most joint methods rely on complex models clinicians cannot interpret. Their approach sets shared cutoffs from differentially private histograms, builds local rules with gradient-boosted trees, and picks sparse weights by regularized optimization. In simulations it matches centralized RuleFit and beats other joint methods, while real data show interpretable results with good accuracy.
arxiv-2604-18756: Saiyed, Sadiekh, and Agarwal test whether pretrained sparse autoencoders make large language models harder to jailbreak. The autoencoders are inserted into transformer residual streams at inference time. With no change to model weights and no blocking of gradients, augmented models cut jailbreak success rates by up to five times versus undefended baselines. Sparser projections defend better, and middle layers best balance defense and clean performance. The pattern fits a bottleneck account: sparse projection reshapes the optimization geometry that jailbreaks exploit.
arxiv-2604-19256: Hernández-Bueno and colleagues introduce QOTPH, a client-side framework for running quantum jobs on a remote server without revealing the data. The client keeps the quantum one-time pad keys and rewrites each operation into a corrected gate. The server then runs the circuit without receiving keys or updating them. The framework covers Clifford operations, rotations, and composed gates, with a global correctness result for circuits built from its verified primitives.
arxiv-2604-19456: Moriya offers a cavity-based scheme using photonic chirality to control braiding and read out non-Abelian anyons in a fractional quantum Hall platform. Counter-propagating cavity modes interfere with a reference tone to create a rotating pinning landscape whose direction follows photon flow. Each light branch thus drives its own anyon loop, making a branch-conditioned braid move mapped onto cavity intermode coherence. The author derives the pinning term and readout relation, and names the operating window: subgap driving and adiabatic transport.
arxiv-2604-19656: Qiu and 11 colleagues tackle a failure mode they call ungrounded reasoning: large language models inventing confident answers when inputs are incomplete. They argue the fault lies not in weak reasoning power. It lies in missing boundary awareness, the skill of noticing when premises needed for a sound inference are absent. Their GRIL method splits reasoning into clarify and pause stages under multi-turn reinforcement learning, training models to ask for missing premises or hold back rather than fabricate.
arxiv-2604-19756: Wei, Wang, and Shi present WorkflowGen, an adaptive tool that builds workflows for language model agents from records of past runs instead of starting fresh each time. Older methods rebuild a workflow from scratch for every query. That drives up cost, slows responses, and weakens robustness. WorkflowGen captures full run records early and extracts reusable knowledge at both step and workflow level, including error fingerprints, best tool matches, parameter schemas, run paths, and ways to avoid exceptions.
arxiv-2604-19856: Eryilmaz presents ChipCraftBrain, a system that turns plain-language specifications into register-transfer-level chip code, the hardware description that defines how circuits move data. Six specialized agents, steered by a learning-based coordinator, split each design into linked sub-modules, solve logic diagrams by algorithm, and verify timing. It reached 97.2 percent on a standard human-written Verilog benchmark and built all eight modules of a RISC-V processor case that passed lint checks on programmable hardware.
arxiv-2604-19956: Aldridge and twenty-three colleagues study intraday Ethereum gas fees using 62,142 confirmed transactions from seven firms in seven industries in early 2026. Fees peak near midday UTC and track speculative arbitrage activity, defying the fee mechanism's assumption of uniform, short-sighted users. Firms respond differently by how easily they can defer trades and how gas-hungry their transactions are. Waste versus perfect off-peak scheduling runs from about 41 to 93 percent of spending, persisting even in the cheapest hours, and the authors map firms onto four scheduling regimes.
arxiv-2604-20156: Shen and Henderson argue expert layers should switch sets far less often, borrowing the options idea from reinforcement learning. Once a model outgrows GPU memory, switching nearly every token kills offloading and prefetch gains. A controller in each layer learns when to switch sets and which to load, built on option-critic learning with deliberation costs. On gpt-oss-20b, low-rank adapters plus a self-taught reward cut switch rates from over 50 percent to below 5 percent. Base accuracy holds up to 90 percent on MATH, MMLU, and MMMLU.
arxiv-2604-20856: Loth, Kappes, and Pahl present CRED-1, an open domain-level credibility dataset built from two openly-licensed source lists plus four computed enrichment signals. The dataset covers 2,672 domains classed as fake, unreliable, mixed, conspiracy, or satire, each with a composite credibility score between 0 and 1. CRED-1 is made for on-device use in privacy-preserving browser extensions to enable client pre-bunking of misinformation at content delivery. The pipeline is built in Python using only standard library modules.
arxiv-2604-21456: Heng Yang casts control design as inference for path and policy tuning under smooth dynamics. Lowering a KL-regularized average path cost yields a Boltzmann-tilted spread over control settings that focuses on low-cost solutions as cooling proceeds. Tempered sequential Monte Carlo anneals samples from a prior to the sharp, multi-peaked target, adjusting weights and resampling with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo refresh using rollout slopes. Policy work pins down the initial-state spread and treats rollout randomness as extra variables; benchmarks show TSMC compares well with rivals.
arxiv-2604-21556: Jingyang Li and three colleagues propose a framework for probability checks of neural networks, computing a guaranteed range for safety odds when inputs follow a distribution, including under disturbances. Three ideas drive it. State-space splitting with regression trees produces chance hulls. Boundary-aware sampling finds the safety boundary in input space for the trees. Iterative refinement uses chance-first ranking. Tests on benchmarks including ACAS Xu and a rocket lander controller show a clear advantage over the state of the art.
arxiv-2604-21656: Sören Wilkening presents a new software backend built for fast quantum circuit generation, aimed at keeping classical preprocessing from eating away any quantum speedup. Benchmarked on the quantum Fourier transform, it builds circuits for systems up to 2000 qubits ahead of popular frameworks like Qiskit and Q#. The package also supplies high-level primitives for bit and integer manipulation, easing integration with higher-level quantum programming languages.
arxiv-2604-21756: Bomisso, Kouma, and Anassé study a coupled nonlinear system linking heat spread, Arrhenius chemistry, and a phase variable, under Neumann boundary conditions. They prove a maximum principle that keeps temperature positive over a time window and keeps inner values within the interval from 0 to 1. In the free regime with no outside push, an energy argument gives local stability of a steady, uniform state.
arxiv-2604-21856: Huang and eight colleagues study radiation and polarisation of fast electrons in a steady magnetic field, with a focus on vortex electrons and their orbital momentum. Transition rates lean one way at low photon energy, favouring a decrease in orbital momentum, like the spin-flip lean in the Sokolov-Ternov effect. Synchrotron radiation can thus polarise orbital momentum. Spin polarisation reaches 92.38 percent, while the orbital kind can approach unity for large values, and its sorting time is orders of magnitude shorter.
arxiv-2604-21956: Valko and four colleagues develop a nonparametric approach to conditional anomaly detection for clinic alerts. It spots data cases with an odd reply, such as a missed important lab test. The method uses the soft harmonic solution to rate label confidence and spot wrong labels. The solution is tuned to avoid flagging lone cases and cases at the edge of data support. It works well at spotting odd labels on a real electronic health record dataset, against several baselines.
arxiv-2604-22156: You and four colleagues introduce Sum-of-Checks, splitting each safety criterion into expert-set reasoning checks. The checks reflect clinical visual evidence. Given a frame, a vision-language model judges each check with a binary verdict and justification, and scores use fixed, weighted aggregation. On Endoscapes2023, Sum-of-Checks beats direct prompting, chain-of-thought, and sub-question splitting, with and without few-shot examples. It lifts frame-level mean average precision by 12 to 14 percent over the best baseline.
arxiv-2604-22256: Zhang and four colleagues tackle goal recognition, inferring an agent's goal from observed behaviour. Real settings add two difficulties: tasks have layered structure, and evidence is uncertain. No earlier planning-based method combined both, the authors say. Their framework works over Hierarchical Task Networks, layered plans, using a planner plus a three-stage model to estimate how likely each goal is. Tests on task-network benchmarks beat the existing recogniser of that type, laying groundwork for more practical goal recognition.
arxiv-2604-22556: Doane-Solomon, Simpson, and Woollings compare two ways to split Central Chile precipitation trends into dynamic and thermodynamic parts. Dynamic change comes from shifting circulation, thermodynamic change from changing moisture, and separating them aids regional understanding and projection. One method uses moisture budget analysis, the other builds constructed circulation analogs, run on CESM2 Large Ensemble fields and two reanalyses. Dynamic trends often differ sharply for single members, though means agree in sign but not size, and analogs applied to budget terms refine historical and future estimates.
arxiv-2604-23056: Xia and Li propose using a one-dimensional Kalman filter for online reward estimation instead of fixed reward normalization in policy gradient reinforcement learning. The filter tracks the latent reward mean step by step, damping noisy returns and adjusting as conditions shift. It adds minimal overhead and needs no changes to existing policy architectures.
